碳酸盐化学的'文石饱和状态'（Ωarag）为何是酸化的关键阈值？

Why is aragonite saturation (Ωarag) the key threshold for acidification?

当Ωarag<1时方解石/文石开始自发溶解。极地海域因冷水溶CO2多已接近或低于Ω=1，珊瑚与翼足类首当其冲；该指标比pH更能直接预示钙化生物的存亡边界。
When Ωarag<1, aragonite begins to dissolve spontaneously. Polar waters, cold and CO2-rich, already approach or drop below Ω=1, hitting corals and pteropods first; this index predicts calcifier survival limits more directly than pH alone.

缺氧（hypoxia）与酸化叠加如何放大对海洋生物的胁迫？

How do hypoxia and acidification jointly amplify stress on marine life?

二者常同源（富营养化与CO2），叠加时钙化能耗上升而缺氧限制代谢供能，使生物在更小范围内同时承受能量赤字与壳溶解，临界氧与pH阈值彼此下移，死亡区扩张更快。
Both often share drivers (eutrophication and CO2); together, calcification costs rise while hypoxia limits metabolic energy, so organisms face energy deficit and shell dissolution at once, with critical O2 and pH thresholds shifting downward and dead zones expanding faster.

海洋酸化为何会最先冲击南大洋和高纬度上升流海域？文石饱和度在其中扮演什么角色？

Why will ocean acidification strike the Southern Ocean and high-latitude upwelling zones first, and what role does the aragonite saturation state play?

海水吸收二氧化碳后碳酸根减少，标志碳酸钙能否稳定存在的文石饱和度Ω随之下降。冷水溶入的CO2多、本底Ω低，故南大洋与北美西岸上升流区的文石不饱和水体会最先升抵海表附近。当Ω低于1时文石趋向溶解，翼足类等薄壳浮游生物造壳受损，而它们是鲑鱼、鲱鱼等的饵料，影响沿食物网上传。
As seawater absorbs CO2, carbonate ions decline and so does the aragonite saturation state Omega that governs whether calcium carbonate can persist. Cold waters hold more CO2 and start with lower Omega, so undersaturated water surfaces earliest in the Southern Ocean and the North American west-coast upwelling zone. Once Omega falls below 1 aragonite tends to dissolve; thin-shelled pteropods cannot build intact shells, and as prey for salmon and herring the damage propagates up the food web.

钙化生物（珊瑚、贝类）为何最怕酸化？

Why are calcifiers like corals and shellfish most hurt by acidification?

它们靠碳酸根构建碳酸钙外壳与骨骼，而酸化降低海水中碳酸根浓度、提高溶解风险，使幼体生长与壳形成变难，进而影响整条食物链。
Calcifiers build shells and skeletons from carbonate; acidification lowers available carbonate and raises dissolution risk, hindering larval growth and shell formation and rippling up the food web.

海洋酸化与全球变暖是同一件事吗？

Is ocean acidification the same as global warming?

不是。变暖是CO2导致热量滞留，酸化是CO2直接溶海改变化学；二者同源但机制不同，且酸化不受短期气温波动影响，是更'确定性'的CO2信号。
No. Warming is heat trapped by CO2; acidification is CO2 dissolving and changing seawater chemistry. Same source, different mechanics, and acidification is unaffected by short-term temperature swings—a more 'certain' CO2 signal.

海洋酸化对翼足类（海螺类）等钙化生物的具体影响机制是什么？

How does ocean acidification specifically affect calcifiers like pteropods?

海水 pH 下降、碳酸根浓度降低，使碳酸钙（特别是霰石）更易溶解，翼足类外壳出现腐蚀孔洞，幼体存活与食物链底层的能量传递受影响。
Lower pH and carbonate ion scarcity make calcium carbonate (especially aragonite) dissolve more easily; pteropod shells develop corrosive pits, hurting larvae and energy flow at the food-web base.

海水变酸和全球变暖是同一个问题的两副面孔?牡蛎养殖户为什么先遭殃?

Ocean acidification and warming are twins? Why did oyster farmers get hit first?

海洋已吸收人类排放二氧化碳的四分之一,溶解后生成碳酸使表层海水pH下降约0.1(氢离子浓度增三成)。受冲击最直接的是钙化生物:碳酸根离子减少,文石饱和度下降,牡蛎与贻贝的幼虫难以建造贝壳。美国西北太平洋的养殖场2007年起幼虫大规模死亡,溯源发现春季上升流把富含CO2的老水送上沿岸孵化场——预警系统让育苗场在低pH时段避峰进水才稳住产业。食物链下游效应仍在展开:珊瑚礁、翼足类与依赖它们的渔业都悬在这条化学曲线上。减排之外,红树林海草的局部碳汇是缓冲带。
Oceans absorbed a quarter of human CO2; dissolved it turns to carbonic acid, dropping surface pH about 0.1 (hydrogen ions up a third). Calcifiers feel it first: carbonate ions thin out, aragonite saturation falls, and oyster mussel larvae struggle to build shells. Pacific Northwest oyster farms saw mass larval deaths from 2007, traced to upwelling delivering CO2-rich deep water to hatcheries — pH early-warning systems timing water intake saved the industry. Food-web ripples spread through corals, pteropods and their fisheries. Beyond emissions cuts, mangrove and seagrass carbon sinks offer local buffering.

海洋为什么会变酸？

Why is the ocean becoming more acidic?

人类排放的CO2约三成被海水吸收，与水反应生成碳酸，释放氢离子使pH下降；虽仍偏碱，但酸化速度在地质史上罕见，威胁钙化生物。
The ocean absorbs about a third of human CO2, which forms carbonic acid and releases hydrogen ions, lowering pH; still alkaline, but the pace of acidification is rare in geologic history and threatens shell-building life.
